precepts.text: For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: the Lord thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth. Does it say equal? It says above.
precepts.point: The Lord their God shall save them in that day as the flock of his people: for they shall be as the stones of a crown, lifted up as an ensign upon his land. Not a brick, not cement: stones of a crown, rubies, jewels. That's how we're going to be.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
“Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope.” The strong hold is the Holy Bible, and we are the prisoners of hope, hoping for New Jerusalem. Some of our people are hoping for equality. We ain't hoping for no damn equality. We are hoping for supremacy, and it is written: “For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: the Lord thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.”

We are holy. We are special unto God. Above. Does it say equal? It says above all people upon the face of the earth. The hell with your equality; we don't want that. Think about the white man's words: when he says we're all equal, what does that translate to? Him on top, we on the bottom. It's all trickery when he speaks.

That is the hope the prisoners hold, and Zechariah shows where it ends. He will raise up “thy sons, O Zion, against thy sons, O Greece”, all twelve tribes against Esau, and make us “as the sword of a mighty man”, transformed from these weak, frail bodies. And “they shall be as the stones of a crown, lifted up as an ensign upon his land”: not a brick, not cement, but rubies and jewels. That is being above, not equal.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.why:
“For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God”, chosen “above all people that are upon the face of the earth.” The nations know that. So they conspire to divide us and go out of their way to make sure we don't reproduce, because we are a problem to these nations: sterilizing our sisters with contraceptive shots, and doctors pressing a needle on an unborn child. Job 13:4 sums up what the Lord says concerning these physicians: “But ye are forgers of lies, ye are all physicians of no value.”

The Bible calls Esau, the white man, a forger of lies. Everything coming out of their mouths is lies. They are physicians of no value: not there to profit you, not there to give you the proper information so you can have a healthy family, an Israelite healthy family. They understand that the strength of the nation starts within the household, so they tell the sisters lies and they tell the husbands lies.

That is Deacon Malachi's experience. At a three-month checkup the doctors said they saw abnormalities and wanted to inject his unborn son to see if he was deformed; the needle could kill the baby, and if he was deformed there was nothing they could do. He was scared, and Satan whispered all kinds of things in his head, but he fasted and prayed, trusted in the Most High, and said to hell with these doctors. They saw his genes and knew who he was. Esau was trying to kill his son Benjamin, and Benjamin is standing in the class today. That is where faith comes in: trust in the Lord and leave everything to the Lord.

So seek counsel from the Lord and from the brothers and sisters set up as medical physicians, the licensed midwives and doulas of the school, before you go to these doctors, so you get a second opinion. What a doctor says is advice, not law. We are above all people in the eyes of God, and the physicians of the nations are not there for our good.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
“For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: the Lord thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself”. He chose you to be special unto him, set apart from everybody else. So the question is: what makes us holy? What scripture?

Leviticus 20:26 was brought from the floor as the answer: “And ye shall be holy unto me: for I the Lord am holy, and have severed you from other people, that ye should be mine.” The Lord is holy, and he severed Israel from other people to be his. That severing is the same set-apart people of Deuteronomy 7:6, chosen “above all people that are upon the face of the earth.”

So there has to be something we are doing that makes us different. We cannot be doing the same thing the world is doing, and we cannot be doing what the churches are doing. What severs us from the other people is the laws of God being applied, which is what Romans 7:12 goes on to show.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
“Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” If the law is holy, and God says you are a holy people, then we are supposed to be a law-abiding people. The laws of God are our constitution, the thing we stand on. That is what makes us holy, what makes us special, what makes us set apart: the laws being applied.

The word of God has no power unless you activate it, and the only way to activate it is to do what it says to do. Other than that it is just pages, just words on a page, just a book. The word is alive and living when you let it live through you by your actions. You become the word, the living example of what it means to be a holy people. That is why the nations say, what a wise and understanding people. They see our actions.

We witness that already at the big events in the big arenas. They say, thousands of black men and nobody smoking weed, no fights breaking out. Then look at what happened in Houston at the rodeo, and how they laughed at us; we are a joke to them. But when we move they ask, how are they so organized, how can they mobilize a few thousand men, put them on the street and file them back in like that, nobody fighting and the place clean? That is the word of God working through us. There is a standard we live by because we are gods on the earth, and it is second nature to us as a nation.

So do not walk in hypocrisy. God gave us something that will make us shine bright and obtain the kingdom. Be that living example to the people.

precepts.why:

They were out in the streets, they did not worship their God, and their own leaders were taking advantage of them at that time.

It is the same in this captivity as in the time of Rome. Look at our people out there: they are lost, they have no shepherd, they are confused. Not only have the people of the world taken advantage of us, but our own people take advantage too, using the knowledge to get preeminence.

So leaders are motivated because we see the same thing Christ saw: our people afflicted, with no leaders, and looking for a shepherd, which is Christ ultimately. Instead of benefiting ourselves, we see the decayed state of our people and make the sacrifices. To hell with the riches, to hell with the women, having sex, and all those other things. We do whatever it takes to rebuild our nation, so that we can truly benefit from each other and have one shepherd rule over us, with nobody able to take advantage of us.

That is the mind the Lord has put in us, and those who carry it are the ones standing in these last days, speaking with authority and showing our people: this is not the way; let us move according to this holy word and restore this nation. That is what it means to be the holy people God chose.

That is the other side of Deuteronomy 7: the Lord “keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations; And repayeth them that hate him to their face, to destroy them”. If you use a position to lead and teach the people and then take advantage of them, beguiling the sisters into sex, keeping them in a filthy mindset, or taking their money, God will judge you. note.label: The Highway of the Upright: an Israelites's Strait Journey

precepts.why:
Deuteronomy 7:6 says the Lord chose Israel “to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.” Deuteronomy 28:1 says it as well, with the condition attached: “if thou shalt hearken diligently unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe and to do all his commandments which I command thee this day, that the Lord thy God will set thee on high above all nations of the earth.”

If God says we are above all people and above all nations, then why can we not do the things we have a concrete visual example of other nations doing, and doing for decades? When one of the Amish gets married, the community comes together and builds a house for that couple, and there is no mortgage attached to it. They do not even have power cars. We have enough knowledge, enough builders, plumbers and concrete men; we can do this too, at a higher level.

It is going to take work to build this kingdom: work, and faith that we can do the work, shown by our actions. We need to fix our credit scores, fix our health, learn group economics, and work together in the trades, so that when the tough times come, losing your job because of your last name or because you are tracked, we have things set up to help each other.

This is the highway of the upright, the Israelite's strait journey. Ezra saw that “A city is builded, and set upon a broad field, and is full of all good things”, but “The entrance thereof is narrow, and is set in a dangerous place to fall”, with fire on the right hand and deep water on the left, and one path “so small that there could but one man go there at once.” That city is the kingdom of heaven, and we must pass through all these things in this captivity to inherit it.

At the end of it, “the ransomed of the Lord shall return, and come to Zion with songs and everlasting joy upon their heads: they shall obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away.” We were ransomed out to the nations, but we are returning and gathering together. Being set on high above all nations is the promise to the people who hearken and do the work.

note.label: Genesis 6: The Sons of God and the Preparing of the Ark

precepts.why:
The men who began to multiply on the face of the earth were of the other nations; they were not the direct descendants of Adam. The sons of God are the lineage of Adam laid out in chapter 5. That is the distinction between the sons of God and the daughters of men, and the sons of God “took them wives of all which they chose.”

The law against marrying into the other nations began right here in Genesis. It was already known. Moses had to reiterate that same law to the children of Israel when they came over Jordan: “Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.” What the sons of God did in Genesis 6 is exactly what Moses forbade.

note.label: Genesis 24: A Wife for Isaac

precepts.why:
The Most High does not deal with marriage into the other nations among His chosen. Moses wrote it plainly: “Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.” But Abraham had his servant swear the same thing long before Moses reiterated it: no wife for Isaac of the daughters of the Canaanites. These laws were in place from the beginning.

The law gives the reason: “For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods: so will the anger of the Lord be kindled against you, and destroy thee suddenly.” Solomon is the prime example. He loved women of the other nations, went into their gods, and had to repent and bring it back.

The forefathers arranged marriages. Abraham sent to his own kindred for Isaac’s wife. The building block of a strong nation is a strong family, and a strong family comes from marriage, not from young men and women left to their own accord.

note.label: Leviticus 25: The Sabbath of the Land and the Year of Jubile

precepts.why:
He brought Israel out of Egypt “to give you the land of Canaan, and to be your God.” This is how He gave it: “When the Lord thy God shall bring thee into the land whither thou goest to possess it, and hath cast out many nations before thee, the Hittites, and the Girgashites, and the Amorites, and the Canaanites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites, seven nations greater and mightier than thou.”

“And when the Lord thy God shall deliver them before thee; thou shalt smite them, and utterly destroy them; thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor shew mercy unto them.” Seven nations greater and mightier than Israel, cast out and delivered before Israel to be smitten, with no covenant and no mercy shewed, during that time period.

He judged Egypt to bring Israel out and cast out the seven nations to give Israel Canaan. The Most High is the God of Israel, not the God of everybody.

precepts.text: Take a wife of the seed of thy fathers; going outside the nation is despising thy brethren in thy heart.
precepts.point: They will turn away thy son from following me: the nations are strangers to the Most High and cannot come into this covenant, so they draw the Israelite spouse off to religions that accept everything. Christianity accepts that union, and that is how they turn you away from your God.

note.label: Deuteronomy 7: A Holy People, Chosen Above All People

precepts.why:
“Beware of all whoredom, my son, and chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father’s tribe: for we are the children of the prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob”. The Most High forbids marrying outside the nation.

The seed of the fathers today is found among the so-called blacks, Hispanics and Native Indians, who make up the twelve tribes of Israel. A spouse may come from any of the twelve tribes, but from within the tribes only. Our fathers from the beginning “all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children, and their seed shall inherit the land.”

“Now therefore, my son, love thy brethren, and despise not in thy heart thy brethren, the sons and daughters of thy people, in not taking a wife of them”. Going outside your nation for a husband or wife is despising your brethren in your heart. Whom you marry is the greatest commitment you make in this life; if you truly loved your people, you would choose one of your own people, “for in pride is destruction and much trouble, and in lewdness is decay and great want: for lewdness is the mother of famine.”

precepts.text: Marriage is taking a sister of thine own people, not for lust but uprightly, to become aged together.
precepts.point: They will turn away thy son from following me: the nations are strangers to the Most High and cannot come into this covenant, so they draw the Israelite spouse off to religions that accept everything. Christianity accepts that union, and that is how they turn you away from your God.

note.label: Deuteronomy 7: A Holy People, Chosen Above All People

precepts.why:
“Thou madest Adam, and gavest him Eve his wife for an helper and stay: of them came mankind: thou hast said, It is not good that man should be alone; let us make unto him an aid like unto himself. And now, O Lord, I take not this my sister for lust but uprightly: therefore mercifully ordain that we may become aged together.”

That is marriage: taking a sister of thine own people, not for lust but uprightly, to become aged together. Whom you marry is the greatest commitment you make in this life, and if you truly loved your people, you would choose one of your own people to become aged together with.

The nations are strangers to the Most High and cannot come into this covenant, so they draw the Israelite spouse off to religions that accept everything. Christianity accepts that union, and that is how “they will turn away thy son from following me”. A wife of thine own people keeps the house in the covenant.

precepts.text: As a man thinketh in his heart, so is he; the heart is the mind, and what is planted there comes out in how you carry yourself.
precepts.point: Being chosen above all people keeps you out of the affairs of this world, their fashions, their hairstyles, their trends and challenges, and keeping up with the Joneses; you cannot flip-flop with every new wave and still carry the speciality the Most High put on you.

note.label: Deuteronomy 7: A Holy People, Chosen Above All People

precepts.why:
“For as he thinketh in his heart, so is he”. The heart is the mind, and what is planted there comes out in how you carry yourself.

That is why “thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God” should be etched into your children's minds from the moment they begin to read, until it is implanted into their spirit. The mind controls the body: what goes into the mind comes out through the body, so a people that knows it is holy and special above all people walks and carries itself differently.

Being chosen above all people keeps you out of the affairs of this world, their fashions, their hairstyles, their trends and challenges, and keeping up with the Joneses. You cannot flip-flop with every new wave and still carry the speciality the Most High put on you. As you think in your heart, so you are.

precepts.text: They departed from Rameses with an high hand in the sight of all the Egyptians; this proves which Pharaoh Israel came out from under.
precepts.point: He kept the oath sworn unto the fathers and redeemed Israel out of the house of bondmen, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt; Israel came out from under Rameses.

note.label: Deuteronomy 7: A Holy People, Chosen Above All People

precepts.why:
“And they departed from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month; on the morrow after the passover the children of Israel went out with an high hand in the sight of all the Egyptians.” This proves which Pharaoh Israel came out from under: Israel came out from under Rameses.

That is the redemption Moses speaks of, “redeemed you out of the house of bondmen, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.” Not because Israel was many, “for ye were the fewest of all people”, only threescore and ten souls out of the loins of Jacob when Israel first went down, but because the Lord loved them and kept the oath sworn unto the fathers. He needs no other reason, and we should never apologize for that.

precepts.text: This is the love of God, that we keep his commandments, and his commandments are not grievous; the opposite of this is how you show him you hate him.
precepts.point: From the jump it has always been the same: love God, keep the commandments; nothing changed between the covenants.

note.label: Deuteronomy 7: A Holy People, Chosen Above All People

precepts.why:
“By this we know that we love the children of God, when we love God, and keep his commandments. For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous.”

This is the same teaching as Moses: the faithful God “keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations”. Loving the Most High is keeping his commandments. And the opposite of this is how you show him you hate him: refusing his commandments shows him with your actions that you hate him, and then judgment comes, for he “repayeth them that hate him to their face, to destroy them”.

From the jump it has always been the same: love God, keep the commandments. Nothing changed between the covenants; John and Moses say the same thing.

precepts.text: Learn not the way of the heathen, and be not dismayed at the signs of heaven; the decked tree is the custom of the people and is vain, and the stargazing, the probes, and the planet colonies are the signs of heaven the heathen are dismayed at.
precepts.point: The main abomination we bring into our house is the Christmas tree of Jeremiah 10: the tree cut down, fastened with nails and hammers, and decked with silver and with gold, whether cut from the forest or bought as a fake tree from the store.

note.label: Deuteronomy 7: A Holy People, Chosen Above All People

precepts.why:
“Hear ye the word which the Lord speaketh unto you, O house of Israel: Thus saith the Lord, Learn not the way of the heathen, and be not dismayed at the signs of heaven; for the heathen are dismayed at them.” The stargazing, the probes and the planet colonies are the signs of heaven the heathen are dismayed at.

“For the customs of the people are vain: for one cutteth a tree out of the forest, the work of the hands of the workman, with the axe. They deck it with silver and with gold; they fasten it with nails and with hammers, that it move not.” That is the Christmas tree, the main abomination we bring into our house, whether cut from the forest or bought as a fake tree from the store. The decked tree is the custom of the people, and it is vain: “They are upright as the palm tree, but speak not: they must needs be borne, because they cannot go.”

Moses said “Neither shalt thou bring an abomination into thine house, lest thou be a cursed thing like it”, and not to desire the silver or gold that is on their gods. Bring it up to today: the Jesus pieces, the crosses, the ankhs and the rosary beads wrapped around the neck and rubbed in prayer make the wearer an abomination and a cursed thing just like the idol, and so does the tree decked with silver and with gold. “Be not afraid of them; for they cannot do evil, neither also is it in them to do good.”

precepts.text: Thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God, chosen to be a special people unto himself, above all people upon the face of the earth.
precepts.point: This is the same word given earlier in Deuteronomy, among other scriptures: thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God, chosen to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.

note.label: Deuteronomy 26: The Firstfruits Confession and a Peculiar People

precepts.why:
“that thou mayest be an holy people unto the Lord thy God, as he hath spoken.” Where had he spoken it? Earlier in Deuteronomy, among other scriptures: “For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: the Lord thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.”

It is the same word: an holy people unto the Lord thy God, chosen above all people that are upon the face of the earth, made high above all nations which he hath made, in praise, and in name, and in honour. As he had spoken it in chapter 7, so he avouched it here.

precepts.text: Make no marriages with the nations of the land, but destroy their altars and burn their graven images with fire.
precepts.point: Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, for the Most High goes with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.

note.label: Deuteronomy 31: Moses' Final Charge and the Rebellion Foretold

precepts.why:
“The Lord thy God, he will go over before thee, and he will destroy these nations from before thee, and thou shalt possess them: and Joshua, he shall go over before thee”. The Most High himself goes over before Israel, and Joshua before the people, and he does to these nations “as he did to Sihon and to Og, kings of the Amorites”. Then: “the Lord shall give them up before your face, that ye may do unto them according unto all the commandments which I have commanded you.”

Which commandments? The guidelines of Deuteronomy 7 for when you enter the land: “Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son. For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods: so will the anger of the Lord be kindled against you, and destroy thee suddenly.” Do not take their daughters for wives or give your sons to theirs, and do not worship their gods.

“But thus shall ye deal with them; ye shall destroy their altars, and break down their images, and cut down their groves, and burn their graven images with fire.” Utterly burn their gods with fire. The nations are given up before Israel's face so that Israel may do exactly this to them. And the charge that goes with it: “Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, nor be afraid of them: for the Lord thy God, he it is that doth go with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.”

precepts.text: Make no covenant with them, neither make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter take unto thy son, for they will turn away thy son from following the Most High to serve other gods, and his anger will destroy thee suddenly.
precepts.point: This is the same thing that happened at Baalpeor, when Israel went and mingled with the women of Moab and then worshipped their gods. The warning here is do not do that thing.

note.label: Joshua 23: Cleave unto the Lord Your God

precepts.why:
“Else if ye do in any wise go back, and cleave unto the remnant of these nations, even these that remain among you, and shall make marriages with them”. Joshua is repeating the law: “thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor shew mercy unto them: Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.”

The reason is given: “For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods: so will the anger of the Lord be kindled against you, and destroy thee suddenly.” This is the same thing that happened at Baalpeor, when Israel went and mingled with the women of Moab and then worshipped their gods. That is why the nations left among you become snares and traps, scourges in your sides and thorns in your eyes, until ye perish from off this good land. The warning here is do not do that thing.

precepts.text: The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire; desire not the gold or silver on them, lest thou be snared therein, for it is an abomination to the Most High.
precepts.point: Because Israel disobeyed, the sentence falls: I will not drive them out from before you, but they shall be as thorns in your sides, and their gods shall be a snare unto you. The people lifted up their voice and wept, called the place Bochim, and sacrificed there unto the Most High.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

precepts.why: Throwing down their altars meant this: “The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire: thou shalt not desire the silver or gold that is on them, nor take it unto thee, lest thou be snared therein: for it is an abomination to the Lord thy God.” Burn them, and do not even desire the silver or gold on them, lest it become a snare. The Most High keeps reiterating that we will be snared and trapped by what these nations serve. Israel did not throw down the altars, and the angel’s sentence was exactly that: “their gods shall be a snare unto you.”

precepts.text: Seven nations greater and mightier than thou: make no covenant with them and no marriages with them, for they will turn away thy son from following me.
precepts.point: Going out to battle against horses and chariots and people more than thou, Israel was told, be not afraid of them, for the Most High is with thee. He constantly repeats these things because he knew we were going to be a stubborn and rebellious people, and he wants us to acknowledge him and only him. Instead Israel did evil, forgat the Most High, and served Baalim and the groves.

note.label: Judges 3: Nations Left to Prove Israel

precepts.why:
Stop and read who Israel is dwelling among: “the Canaanites, Hittites, and Amorites, and Perizzites, and Hivites, and Jebusites.” Are those not the same people the Most High said to utterly destroy? Deuteronomy 7 names them: “the Hittites, and the Girgashites, and the Amorites, and the Canaanites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites, seven nations greater and mightier than thou.” And the commandment was, “thou shalt smite them, and utterly destroy them; thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor shew mercy unto them.” But we are dwelling among them.

The law said it plainly about the marriages too: “Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.” Judges 3 records the exact opposite: “they took their daughters to be their wives, and gave their daughters to their sons, and served their gods.”

The reason was given beforehand: “For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods: so will the anger of the Lord be kindled against you, and destroy thee suddenly.” That is precisely what happened. Israel “forgat the Lord their God, and served Baalim and the groves.”

precepts.text: The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire; desire not the silver or gold on them, lest thou be snared.
precepts.point: The Philistines left their images there, and David and his men burned them. David knew the law, that the graven images of the nations were to be burned with fire and their silver and gold not desired, lest a man be snared and cursed by bringing an abomination into his house.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

precepts.why:
At Baal-perazim “they left their images, and David and his men burned them.” David knew the law: “The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire: thou shalt not desire the silver or gold that is on them, nor take it unto thee, lest thou be snared therein: for it is an abomination to the Lord thy God.”

He did not keep the Philistines' gods as spoil or desire the silver and gold on them. He burned them, exactly as the law commanded, lest a man be snared by them.

precepts.text: Bring not an abomination into thine house; utterly detest and abhor it, for it is a cursed thing.
precepts.point: The Philistines left their images there, and David and his men burned them. David knew the law, that the graven images of the nations were to be burned with fire and their silver and gold not desired, lest a man be snared and cursed by bringing an abomination into his house.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

precepts.why:
The law goes on: “Neither shalt thou bring an abomination into thine house, lest thou be a cursed thing like it: but thou shalt utterly detest it, and thou shalt utterly abhor it; for it is a cursed thing.”

That is why David and his men burned the images the Philistines left behind. To carry them home would have brought an abomination into the house and made a man a cursed thing like it. David knew the law and kept it, even in the heat of victory.

precepts.text: Israel is a holy people whom the Most High chose to be a special people above all people on the face of the earth.
precepts.point: She blessed the Most High who delighted in Solomon to set him on the throne of Israel, because the Most High loved Israel forever; even the nations understood that the Most High chose Israel above all people.

note.label: 1 Kings 10: The Queen of Sheba and the Riches of Solomon

precepts.why:
“For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: the Lord thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.”

Even the nations understood that the Most High chose Israel above all people. The queen of Sheba said it herself: “Blessed be the Lord thy God, which delighted in thee, to set thee on the throne of Israel: because the Lord loved Israel for ever, therefore made he thee king, to do judgment and justice.”

She saw it in Solomon's servants too: “Happy are thy men, happy are these thy servants, which stand continually before thee, and that hear thy wisdom.” They were happy to be in order, serving with joyfulness and not complaining, because Solomon ruled wisely and took care of his people.

precepts.text: He set his love on Israel not because they were many but because he loved them and kept the oath to their fathers.
precepts.point: She blessed the Most High who delighted in Solomon to set him on the throne of Israel, because the Most High loved Israel forever; even the nations understood that the Most High chose Israel above all people.

note.label: 1 Kings 10: The Queen of Sheba and the Riches of Solomon

precepts.why:
“The Lord did not set his love upon you, nor choose you, because ye were more in number than any people; for ye were the fewest of all people: But because the Lord loved you, and because he would keep the oath which he had sworn unto your fathers, hath the Lord brought you out with a mighty hand”.

He set his love on Israel not because they were many, but because he loved them and kept the oath to their fathers. That is the love the queen of Sheba spoke of: “because the Lord loved Israel for ever, therefore made he thee king”.

precepts.text: Make no marriages with the other nations, for they will turn away thy son from following the Most High.
precepts.point: He had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines, and his wives turned away his heart. It happened exactly as the Most High said it would, for the law had warned that intermarriage would turn the heart to serve other gods, and it was not a maybe but a will.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

precepts.why:
“Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.” Make no marriages with the other nations, for they will turn away thy son from following the Most High.

Solomon loved “women of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Zidonians, and Hittites”, the very nations of which the Most High said, “Ye shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in unto you: for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods”. It was not a maybe but a will. “Solomon clave unto these in love”, and “his wives turned away his heart.” It happened exactly as the Most High said it would.

precepts.text: Israel is not to marry outside the people, lest their hearts be turned to other gods.
precepts.point: In his days Hiel of Bethel rebuilds Jericho, laying its foundation in his firstborn Abiram and setting up its gates in his youngest Segub, according to the word spoken by Joshua.

note.label: 1 Kings 16: Baasha to Ahab and the Rise of Baal Worship

precepts.why:
The law forbids it: “Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.” Israel is not to marry outside the people, lest their hearts be turned to other gods.

Ahab broke that law, and it did exactly what the law warned. As if walking in the sins of Jeroboam were a light thing, he married Jezebel, the daughter of the king of the Zidonians, and went and served Baal. Solomon’s wives turned his heart after Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Zidonians; Jezebel turned Ahab’s heart to Baal.

precepts.text: The graven images of their gods shall be burned with fire as a cursed and abominable thing.
precepts.point: After the sacrifice he sends in the guard to slay them all, breaks down the images and the house of Baal, and makes it a draught house, so Jehu destroyed Baal out of Israel.

note.label: 2 Kings 10: Jehu Destroys Baal and Falls Short of the Law

precepts.why:
“The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire.” The silver and gold on them is not to be desired, “for it is an abomination to the Lord thy God.” It is not to be brought into the house, “lest thou be a cursed thing like it: but thou shalt utterly detest it, and thou shalt utterly abhor it; for it is a cursed thing.”

That is the law Jehu carried out. He gathered all the worshippers of Baal in subtilty, filled the house of Baal, and after the sacrifice sent in the guard to slay them. Then “they brought forth the images out of the house of Baal, and burned them. And they brake down the image of Baal, and brake down the house of Baal, and made it a draught house unto this day.”

The images were burned with fire and treated as the cursed thing they are. So Jehu destroyed Baal out of Israel.

precepts.text: The graven images of their gods are to be burned with fire, and their silver and gold not desired, for it is a cursed and abominable thing to bring into the house.
precepts.point: When Josiah read the law the fear of the Lord came upon him and he saw why the nation was under judgment, just as a person is cut when they first hear the truth and realize what they have been doing wrong.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

precepts.why:
“The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire: thou shalt not desire the silver or gold that is on them”, “for it is an abomination to the Lord thy God. Neither shalt thou bring an abomination into thine house, lest thou be a cursed thing like it.”

Judah had brought the abomination into the very house of the Lord: “all the vessels that were made for Baal, and for the grove, and for all the host of heaven.” Josiah had them brought forth out of the temple, “and he burned them without Jerusalem in the fields of Kidron, and carried the ashes of them unto Beth–el.”

When Josiah read the law, the fear of the Lord came upon him and he saw why the nation was under judgment. He did what the law said to do with the cursed thing: burn it with fire and get it out of the house.

precepts.text: Their graven images are to be burned so they do not become a snare unto us.
precepts.point: The Philistine gods left there were burned with fire.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 14: David Established and Inquiring of the Most High

precepts.why:
“The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire: thou shalt not desire the silver or gold that is on them, nor take it unto thee, lest thou be snared therein: for it is an abomination to the Lord thy God.” Their images are to be burned so they do not become a snare unto us.

David kept this. He smote the Philistines at Baal-perazim and said, “God hath broken in upon mine enemies by mine hand like the breaking forth of waters”, naming the place for it. “And when they had left their gods there, David gave a commandment, and they were burned with fire.”

precepts.text: Make no marriages with the nations, for they turn the heart to other gods; instead destroy their altars, break their images, and burn their groves.
precepts.point: This obeyed the law directly: rather than intermarry with the nations, Israel was to destroy their altars and burn their graven images.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 31: The Tithe Restored

precepts.why:
“Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son. For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods”. Make no marriages with the nations, for they turn the heart to other gods.

Instead: “thus shall ye deal with them; ye shall destroy their altars, and break down their images, and cut down their groves, and burn their graven images with fire.”

That is the law Israel obeyed directly when the feast was finished. They “went out to the cities of Judah, and brake the images in pieces, and cut down the groves, and threw down the high places and the altars out of all Judah and Benjamin, in Ephraim also and Manasseh, until they had utterly destroyed them all.” Then every man returned “to his possession, into their own cities”, the reformation now reaching beyond the temple into the whole land.

precepts.text: The graven images of the nations were to be burned with fire and not desired, for they are an abomination to the Most High, the example Manasseh follows in casting down the idols.
precepts.point: He repairs the altar of the Lord, sacrifices peace offerings and thank offerings on it, and commands Judah to serve the Lord God of Israel, though the people still sacrifice in the high places, only unto the Lord their God.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 33: Manasseh's Wickedness and His Humbling

precepts.why:
“The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire: thou shalt not desire the silver or gold that is on them, nor take it unto thee, lest thou be snared therein: for it is an abomination to the Lord thy God.” The graven images of the nations were to be destroyed and not desired, for they are an abomination to the Most High.

That is the example Manasseh followed once he was humbled. “And he took away the strange gods, and the idol out of the house of the Lord, and all the altars that he had built in the mount of the house of the Lord, and in Jerusalem, and cast them out of the city.” He kept none of it.

Then “he repaired the altar of the Lord, and sacrificed thereon peace offerings and thank offerings, and commanded Judah to serve the Lord God of Israel.” He also built the wall of the city of David and “put captains of war in all the fenced cities of Judah.” The people still sacrificed in the high places, “yet unto the Lord their God only.”

precepts.text: The commandment was to make no marriages with the nations, not giving daughters to their sons nor taking their daughters, because they would turn the children away from following the Most High.
precepts.point: The sin is interracial marriage with the nations, taking their daughters for themselves and their sons, so that the holy seed mingled itself with the people of those lands. It was not only the common people but the Levites, the leaders, that were chief in this trespass.

note.label: Ezra 9: Ezra Mourns the Strange Wives

precepts.why:
The princes told Ezra that Israel, the priests and the Levites “have not separated themselves from the people of the lands”, taking “of their daughters for themselves, and for their sons: so that the holy seed have mingled themselves with the people of those lands.” The sin is interracial marriage with the nations, the Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Ammonites, Moabites, Egyptians and Amorites, and the princes and rulers were chief in it.

The commandment they broke is in Deuteronomy: “Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.” The reason is given too: “For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods: so will the anger of the Lord be kindled against you, and destroy thee suddenly.”

That is why it is a trespass and not a small matter. Marrying the nations turns the children away from following the Most High to serve other gods, and it kindles his anger to destroy suddenly. It was not only the common people but the Levites and the leaders who had done it.

precepts.text: The law forbids marrying the nations because they will turn the son away from following the Most High to serve other gods, and kindle his anger to destroy them.
precepts.point: Because the fathers were not truly in the house, the children learned their mother's tongue and customs instead of Hebrew and the law. Nehemiah contended with them, cursed them, smote certain of them, plucked off their hair, and made them swear not to give or take daughters in marriage with those nations, reminding them that Solomon himself, though beloved of his God, was caused to sin by outlandish women.

note.label: Nehemiah 13: Cleansing the People, the Sabbath, and the Strange Wives

precepts.why:
Nehemiah saw Jews that had married wives of Ashdod, Ammon and Moab, and their children “spake half in the speech of Ashdod, and could not speak in the Jews’ language”. The law forbade this from the beginning: “Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son. For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods: so will the anger of the Lord be kindled against you, and destroy thee suddenly.”

The reason is given in the law: they will turn the son away from following the Most High to serve other gods, and his anger will be kindled to destroy them suddenly. Because the fathers were not truly in the house, the children learned their mother's tongue and customs instead of Hebrew and the law, the very turning away the law warned of. That is why Nehemiah made them swear, “Ye shall not give your daughters unto their sons, nor take their daughters unto your sons”.
